about: The block-by-block workshop's first round of crit, from the walk-in to the end of the demo (m001 to m031), as Noah left it on October 20, 2026, before the boards were cleared for round two. His notes are also in design/history/data/compass.js, word for word; what was built from them is entries 225 to 231. The moments were re-recorded after this round with the same IDs.

notes.m001: For the initial walk in, lets have a fun, colorful, extremely bold way of showing our names and school. It should say "Cooper Union School of Art". Take away "Color palette". No fade in, and it should be pretty huge as we walk in, covering the screen. "Noah" should come first, then "Daeun", on the screen at the same time. Then they are replaced by a large "Cooper Union School of Art" text. Colors, you decide. Whatever looks great with our footage. Same font and spacing - looks beautiful.
notes.m002: Daeun and I sit down, before I say my first line. I'd like to keep this, as almost a quick cut/transition into our interview-styled introductions.
notes.m003: This whole section where we offer the introduction should remain uncut
notes.m006: The exact moment I say "Palit", that should cue the splash
notes.m007: Can the splash be a little more creative? Maybe the colored squares come together, starting and fading in as whole squares, then have a subtraction effect as they begin to touch and merge? After all, the logo is supposed to be two color cards coming together. The way the text appears isn't that subtle or interesting either. Maybe it slides out from the icon? Just a suggestion - but will follow your guidance. Refer to the motion graphics I did for the Kino brandmark if possible - the splash should be fun and witty. The logo itself could be bigger compared to the text.
notes.m009: I'm wondering how we can be a little bolder, and a little more creative with these transitional overlays. Could we perhaps play with how the highlighted word appears or comes to be? Or, how the words even appear on the page in general? Right now, we have a fade in that doesn't feel very authentic or interesting - something with slightly more movement and speed may be the move. Keep this in mind for all future overlays.
notes.m010: Not loving the centred nature of the brief. And, not loving how each word fades in. Could we try line by line instead? And I'm curious to know how we can make the highlighting a little more authentic. Feels a little stale right now
notes.m011: Could we integrate some color into this rep? for such an important moment, it feels a little matter of fact, or gray
notes.m013: Some colors are a little too close to gray or white to be able to be distinguished from the background. Just slightly. Could we make them a little more punchy? Not ugly though. I also don't like how the colors appear - they just randomly fade in, which seems to be a common theme through the video. Why don't we try this - the screen fills with a grid of these colors, then we zoom out to see the visualization and the header, then they fill in to resolve the statistic. Love the showing of the research citing
notes.m014: Firstly, the script makes it hard to understand what that means - can we simplify the language, and tune it so that its more research focused? The line is already doing a good job at that, but i think we could be clearer. And, the representation doesn't mean anything. Can we instead show the actual references on the screen, then drop the 6 that don't lead anywhere?
notes.m015:
The header should frame alikeness as negative: "...stories got more creative, but more alike"

This data viz does well for what it means. Maybe as we rebuild the video, we can get inspired by the new visual language being created, then change this specific line accordingly?
notes.m016:
We need to acknowledge our references, such as pantone, specimen cards, and why. What research and deliberate research led us in this direction? Is this the right place to put this information? In any case, we need to make that important, tying to what palit sells in this realm.

I keep seeing this basic, static fade-in we use in this video. Why don't we put components like the Pantone line first, as a main header, then we push another line upwards, ie Palit sells ownership, and as the initial pantone line gets pushed upwards, it shrinks. That already is such an improvement from our stagnant showing of the text. Keep this method, as well as others in mind.
notes.m018: Instead of the blocks slowly appearing, could we have the key words appear as colored words on the rightside, beside the card, then at the end, they fall, then the blocks appear much faster? To show how the value are what goes into a palette for a project. This will also pair nicely with the next slide
notes.m020: the connecting line feels a little thin, and a little too dark. For the overlay, refer to the first overlay's notes.
notes.m022: Why do we hover/click the icon at first? Why don't we start with the full screen zoomed into the icon at the icon at the top, then we zoom out into the desktop?
notes.m023: This is nice, but the keybinds showing could be prettier. Like they appear in the order you click them in, and show for just a little longer for the viewers to see. Just a little. Also loving the following of the mouse - could we actually even zoom in a little more?
notes.m024: After the user clicks the color that they want to keep, I think it would be nice if we had a very short pause and a beat. The camera quickly switches to the side chip, and then the side chip reacts as the color lands. I know the actual tool doesn't do that, but I wanted to animate it nicely just to accentuate the actual feature itself. We should also visit the chip first and see that change first before we see the top bar change as well. The chip bumps, and the mouse follows, to show that it was recorded, then, the we pan to the top bar, where we see that the icon bumps too, adopting the chosen color. Let's be extremely mindful of what's on our window and what we can immediately see when we're giving these demos. I think that's extremely important.
notes.m025: This demo happens a little bit faster than I'd like it to. The mouse is very much all over the place really quickly. I think it could take just a little bit more time to be smoother. Maybe have rounder paths to get to where it's going, like how a real user would use a mouse, not just going in a straight line from point A to point B. More intentional framing of what we're following, like the mouse and whatnot. Maybe a little bit zoomed in, just a little bit more, and kind of more timing as we see what the features are and how they're using it in the demo
notes.m026:
This is great, showing how the dashboard looks when you first open it. Honestly, I think just making things a little slower, even if they're not that slow, in the actual app itself could be helpful. For example, when you click today, things fade into what it would look like in the hunt of that day.

I also don't really like how the colors in today just jump to where they should be when the screen changes. Let's change that so they very elegantly and quickly fade out, but then quickly fade back into where they should be, with just a little bit of movement: not too much, not too quick or jagged, but taking time and being elegant.
notes.m027: Same feedback for the previous section. When you open the zoom, it should be a little bit more elegant in how the animations play, how we see that happen, and the fade-in.
notes.m028: We could make the Spectrum's scroll a little bit more human. It still looks like a bot did it, or it's very linear in how it scrolls. Again, a little bit more time, or even just more distinction between what you're actually doing when you're exploring this area. Our beats and timing matter so much - please keep this in mind.
notes.m029: this is good, just refer to prior notes regarding timing
notes.m030: refer to prior notes regarding timing - seems to be a bit of a pain point in this section
notes.m031: refer to prior notes regarding timing
